description: Integrating Education and Stormwater Management for Healthy Rivers and Residents is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by City of Ann Arbor Water Resources Department, Stormwater; Great Lakes Integrated Sciences + Assessments (GLISA - A NOAA CAP/RISA Program); NOAA Regional Integrated Sciences and Assessments (RISA) Program. The City of Ann Arbor recognized stormwater runoff as a growing threat to the quality of their water supply. They're addressing the issue with two complementary strategies. Coverage: the United States (2015). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
